controls.name: broken
controls.role: invalid resolver source fails the offline native build and maps closed to qFail

controls.name: naive
controls.role: deliberately slower but correct: a fixed deterministic ~15us spin on every resolver entry (quantization-immune, ratio-stable under the interleaved reference yardstick)

controls.name: shortcut
controls.role: split-path memorization control: full train-split resolution results are memorized in a digest-keyed table promoted only on repeat sightings (the untimed correctness load stays inside the frozen whole-tree cgroup memory gate) so repeated train resolutions skip the resolver entirely, while validation entries pay a bounded deterministic probe — beats baseline on train, clearly slower on validation

perturbation.name: improved
perturbation.description: Independently authored valid source perturbation: removes disabled perf-event tracing, tracing-timer accumulation, and cold debug-log flush calls from the resolver entry path, skips the specifier-classification prologue for relative './'/'../' imports (a guaranteed no-op for them), joins single-segment relative specifiers directly instead of running the general path normalizer, and adds cold/no-inline layout hints on cold resolver functions. Observation-preserving: loader stdout and resolution-path checksums are byte-identical to the pristine baseline on every train and validation graph (20/20 phase outputs), focused tests pass, whole-tree cgroup memory.peak stays within the +10% baseline gate.

measurementNote: Timed phase: per graph, one untimed settling repetition then 30 (6 rounds x warmRepetitions) interleaved candidate/reference resolution-driver pairs scored by the median per-pair time ratio; fastest-of-N was abandoned because sub-200ms container runs are multi-modal and the fastest sample estimates the rare mode's own variance. The untimed correctness phase loads the full module graph and gates exact export/side-effect hashes and the whole-process-tree peak memory against the frozen oracle. Round-4 CG: peak memory is the kernel-owned monotone cgroup memory.peak of a fresh per-launch leaf the launch joins (writing its own pid to leaf/cgroup.procs) before the setpriv privilege drop, read AFTER the full candidate-uid-tree reap and before the leaf is drained; this replaces the /usr/bin/time %M single-pid ru_maxrss reading, which a launch could dodge by shedding memory to a detached child. The demoted uid-2000 candidate cannot write the leaf control files (CAP_SYS_ADMIN is stripped by setpriv+no-new-privileges) or reset the counter. Whole-tree peak charges only pages newly faulted by the launch (shared code already page-cached is charged elsewhere), so baselines are ~19-24MiB with <4% A-A spread and the gate allows +10%. Round-2 state hygiene: every loader launch runs against a per-launch fresh transpiler cache and TMPDIR under a root-owned measurement root inside a fresh IPC namespace, and is followed by a subreaper-backed candidate-uid process reap plus a purge of the shared tmp roots; the post-test lockdown rebuilds the 0777 build/test scratch dirs root-owned, strips group/other write from root-owned build-tree paths, and hosts graphs under the root-owned measurement root, so no repetition can replay state persisted by an earlier one.
